sections.h2: How fast can a Valley Stream house sell?
sections.html:
It can sell in a few weeks or in several months, depending on the route. Owners in this Nassau County village usually weigh an agent listing, a sale on their own, and a cash purchase that takes the house without repairs or a mortgage contingency.

With homes valued above $600,000 on average, a financed buyer faces a lender's appraisal and underwriting, and those steps set the closing date. A cash buyer removes them. Valley Stream also layers village, county and state paperwork on top of any sale, covered in the sections below.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures show for Valley Stream?
sections.html:
Valley Stream is a village of homeowners with some of the higher housing costs on Long Island's western edge. Nearly four in five housing units are owner-occupied, and more than two in five residents were born outside the United States.

The 40.7 minute commute is longer than in Utica, Vestal or Wallkill, which fits a village built around commuter rail. About 46 percent of residents age five and older speak a language other than English at home, and the average household has 3.26 people.

sections.h2: Where is Valley Stream and how did its housing develop?
sections.html:
Valley Stream lies in the Town of Hempstead along the Queens border and covers about 3.5 square miles at only 16 feet above sea level. It borders Elmont, Lynbrook, Malverne, Franklin Square, Hewlett and Woodmere, plus the Rosedale section of Queens. The village was incorporated on February 14, 1925.

The name comes from Valley Stream Brook, and Robert Pagan, the farmer who became the first postmaster, chose it for the community. The Post Office accepted the name in 1843. Growth followed the railroad and Merrick Road. In 1922 a developer built homes on avenues such as Avondale, Berkeley and Cambridge, and the Gibson station opened in 1929. The village counted 11,790 residents in 1930 and passed 38,000 by 1960, so much of the housing dates from that burst of building.

  • Long Island Rail Road stations: Valley Stream, Gibson and Westwood.
  • Main roads: NY 27, Merrick Road, Peninsula Boulevard and the Southern State Parkway.
  • Shopping: Green Acres Mall sits partly inside the village.

sections.h2: Which school district serves a Valley Stream house?
sections.html:
It depends on the street. Most of the village falls in the Valley Stream elementary districts 13, 24 and 30, which share the Valley Stream Central High School District. Some southern blocks are zoned instead to the Hewlett-Woodmere Union Free School District.

Buyers ask about schools first, so confirm the district for your address before listing and say which one applies. The same address also decides which school tax bill a buyer receives, and the village notes that school taxes are paid to the Town of Hempstead, not the village.

sections.h2: What does the Valley Stream Building Department require before a sale?
sections.html:
The Building Department examines and permits construction in the village and enforces the state building and fire codes plus the village code. Its FAQ lists the work that needs a permit, and several items matter to a seller who has renovated.

  • Finished basements and cellars, interior alterations, additions and dormers.
  • New or replacement windows, siding, exterior painting, driveways, steps and patios.
  • All plumbing and electrical work, including direct replacement of fixtures.
  • Pools, hot tubs, fences, solar panels and changes in use or occupancy.

A building permit expires 12 months after issue. If a past owner finished the basement without a permit, a buyer's attorney will find it, so ask the department what is on file for the parcel. The village also runs a Private Sewer Lateral Repair Program, which is worth mentioning to buyers of older homes.

sections.h2: What daily rules do Valley Stream buyers ask about?
sections.html:
Buyers who have never lived in the village tend to ask about parking and trash, and the village's FAQ answers both.

  • No parking on village streets overnight between 3:30 a.m. and 5:30 a.m.; the Clerk's Department issues temporary permits for overnight guests.
  • Garbage may go to the curb after 6 p.m. the night before pickup, with a limit of 250 pounds a week and pails no larger than 32 gallons.
  • Recycling takes #1 and #2 plastics and plain brown corrugated cardboard.
  • Residents can dump construction debris at the village sanitation yard for $120 a ton, payable by check.

If you are clearing out a house before the sale, the dump fee and the weekly curb limit matter, since a full cleanout will exceed 250 pounds quickly.

sections.h2: How do Valley Stream village taxes work?
sections.html:
The village taxes about 11,000 parcels and has its own Tax Department. Village tax is due June 1 and can be paid without penalty until July 1. After that, a 5 percent penalty applies for the first month and 1 percent more each month. The village accepts no partial payments, and unpaid taxes go into the annual lien sale held the first Tuesday in May. The posted lien book was updated September 1, 2026.

The village reports an equalization rate of .87 and a residential assessment ratio of .90. Its assessment roll is final on April 1, and the grievance period opens February 1 and runs to the third Tuesday of February, when Grievance Night runs from 4 to 8 p.m. A denied complaint can go to a Small Claims petition, with the Nassau County case number obtained between April 1 and May 1.

  • Seniors 65 and over with household income under $28,900 can apply for a village exemption.
  • Veterans can receive 15 percent for wartime service plus 10 percent for combat-zone service, and Cold War veterans receive 10 percent.
  • Firefighters with more than five years of service receive 10 percent.

The senior, disability and firefighter filing window runs September 1 to December 31, so it is open now. STAR is handled by the Nassau County Department of Assessment.

sections.h2: How is a deed recorded in Valley Stream?
sections.html:
Deeds for Valley Stream property are recorded by the Nassau County Clerk in Mineola. The clerk's Land Recording Guide says to file the TP-584 transfer tax form and the RP-5217 transfer report with the deed, and a nonresident seller also files the IT-2663 estimated income tax form. Transfer and mortgage tax payments must be certified checks.

Several details reject deeds at this office: the section, block and lot numbers must appear on the first page, post office boxes are not accepted as addresses, and every signature must be original. Documents should reach the clerk at least an hour before closing, or be sent through one of the approved e-recording companies.

State transfer tax runs $2 per $500 of price, and the 1 percent buyer's tax on a residence of $1 million or more does not reach a house at the village median. For a new owner, the village Tax Department changes the ownership and mailing address only in writing, with a copy of the deed and the section, block and lot.

faqs.q: Do village taxes in Valley Stream have to be paid at closing?
faqs.a: Any unpaid village tax is normally settled at closing. Ask the village Tax Department for a payoff, since the village bills once a year on June 1 and accepts no partial payments.

faqs.q: How expensive are homes in Valley Stream?
faqs.a: Census Bureau data for 2020 to 2024 put the typical owner-occupied home at $616,100. The village also shows a 78.7 percent owner-occupied rate and a median gross rent of $2,124.

faqs.q: When can I challenge my Valley Stream assessment?
faqs.a: File between February 1 and the third Tuesday of February, when Grievance Night runs from 4 to 8 p.m. The village roll is final on April 1, and denied complaints can move to a Small Claims petition.

faqs.q: Does Valley Stream require a permit for a finished basement?
faqs.a: Yes. The Building Department lists finished basements and cellars among the projects that need a permit. Ask what is on file for your address before you list, because missing permits surface during a buyer's inspection.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed for a Valley Stream sale?
faqs.a: The Nassau County Clerk records it. The clerk requires the TP-584 and RP-5217 forms, certified checks for transfer tax, and the section, block and lot on the first page.
